passages.original: Θεόπομπος ἀναγράφει δὲ ταύτης τὴν θέσιν,
passages.notes: Single verse line without context; 'its' refers to an unidentified place.

passages.english: we shall set out all [of them] by nation, following Ephorus
passages.notes: 'ἅπόντας' is evidently a scanning error for 'ἅπαντας' (all); translated accordingly.

passages.original: αὐτῶν Ἔφορος εἴρηκεν, εἶναί φησί τε
passages.english: Ephorus has spoken of them, and he says that [it/they] is
passages.notes: Fragmentary single line; the sentence continues beyond the passage.

passages.english: Herodotus records these things in his history.
passages.notes: Verse (iambic trimeter) in the original; rendered as a single line.

passages.english: Ephorus has said, then the Aroteres beyond
passages.notes: 'εἶλτεν' is unintelligible as printed; probably a scanning error for 'εἶτ᾽ ἐν' or 'εἶτα' ('then'). Translated as 'then'. Aroteres ('Ploughmen') is taken as the name of a people.

passages.original: ὡς δʼ Ἔφορος ἱστόρηκεν, ἐκ λίμνης τινός,
passages.english: and as Ephorus has reported, from a certain lake,

passages.original: ὁ συγγραφεὺς εἴρηκεν, ὡς δʼ Ἔφορος λέγει
passages.english: the historian has said, and as Ephorus says
passages.notes: 'The historian' is unidentified in this isolated line.

passages.original: Ὁ δ᾿ Ἡρόδοτος ἔοικεν ἀγνοεῖν, λέγων
passages.english: But Herodotus seems to be unaware [of this], saying
